text:
maria: FYI I noticed a BERTScore dip after the INT8 quant rollout on the new runner, dashboard spike in calibration curve.
ashok: which exact BERTScore variant? F1, precision, recall? link?
maria: F1 mainly. dash: https://dash.redwood/metrics/bertscore/canary — baseline ~0.875 -> post-quant ~0.823.
devon: did we change tokenization/detoken anywhere in quant pipeline? that would wreck embedding-based scores.
maria: tokenization unchanged. pass@k & exact-match stable, so likely a scoring math bug.
ci-bot: build failed: tests/metrics/test_bertscore.py::test_calibration — AssertionError 0.823 != 0.875
ashok: paste failing log snippet?
maria: sure:
```
E   AssertionError: 0.823 != 0.875
E   Diff: -0.052
File: eval/metrics/bertscore.py line 212
Stack: eval/runner/aggregator.py:47 -> eval/metrics/bertscore.py:212
```
sylvia: I recall a previous INT8 path bug: accumulators were left as int32 and division used integer semantics in one codepath. small negative bias possible.
devon: looking at the quant kernel wrapper: int8 kernel returns int32 sums, then aggregator does `score = total_sum / lengths` but in the quant runner that code sometimes has `total_sum` as np.int32 and `lengths` np.int64 -> numpy may do integer division depending on types.
nashok: yep numpy behavior here can floor when both operands are integer dtype. cast ordering matters. quick fix: cast to float before division.
maria: example patch suggestion:
```diff
- score = total_sum // lengths
+ score = total_sum.astype(np.float64) / lengths.astype(np.float64)
```
devon: I'll add a unit test that simulates int-path to catch regressions. also check C-level kernel: if it reduces into int32, make sure we expose float to python.
sylvia: can we add a small calibration smoke check in the runner CI? generate synthetic logits with known calibration curve and assert within epsilon.
maria: please do. also add a short note to the dashboard alert config to increase threshold temporarily to avoid noisy pages while we patch.
eval-bot: created issue RED-ML-2417: "BERTScore: integer division in INT8 scoring path causes calibration and F1 bias" assigned to @devon.
ci-bot: re-run requested by @devon
devon: pushing fix branch fix/bertscore-intcast, adding test that fails on master. will monitor canary and re-run smoke.
maria: if canary still shows drift we should revert scoring to float kernel for now until optimized kernel patch lands.
nashok: agreed. I'll update rollout policy to prefer float-scoring for tasks with eval=true.
sylvia: filed follow-up RED-ML-2418 for pass@k tiny drop after dedup ordering change — lower priority.
maria: thanks. once PR merges, please post canary metrics so we can close alerts. :thumbsup:
